name: Costa Rican Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Highlands of southwestern costa rica and western panama (chiriquí)
description: Medium-sized sparrowlike bird with green back, gray eyebrow, black cheek, and white throat. Most similar to Black-striped Sparrow but with entire cheek black (not just eyeline); also compare with Chestnut-capped Brushfinch but note lack of rufous crown.

name: Samoan Myzomela
rangeDescription: Samoa (upolu, savai'i, and tutuila)
description: A small, strikingly plumaged myzomela with a bright crimson-red head, chest, back, and rump and black wings, belly, and tail. Thin bill decurved.

name: Pacific Golden-Plover
rangeDescription: Winters from eastern africa southward through asia and the tropical pacific to australia and new zealand
description: Slender plover spangled with gold. Breeding plumage shows black belly and face with mottled white sides and undertail coverts and a white stripe down the side of the neck that continues onto the sides of the chest and flanks.

name: White Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Dry forest of south america east of the andes to northern argentina
description: Strikingly-plumaged medium-sized woodpecker, mostly white with dark wings and back contrasting with yellow goggles with a dark eye stripe. Males have a yellowish nape.

name: Nilgiri Flowerpecker
rangeDescription: Western ghats and coastal southwestern india
description: Small plain gray-brown bird with a slightly curved bill. Nearly identical to Plain Flowerpecker, but ranges do not overlap.

name: Tiny Tyrant-Manakin
rangeDescription: Southeastern venezuela to the guianas and northeastern amazonian brazil
description: Tiny, short-tailed denizen of tall rainforest; common, but heard far more often than seen. Virtually devoid of good field marks, since male’s yellow crown patch is rarely seen from below.

name: Oriental Stork
rangeDescription: Siberia, manchuria, and korea; winters to southern china and northern india
description: Endangered stork of expansive wetlands and fields in East Asia. Adult white with sharply contrasting black flight feathers, black bill, and red legs; juvenile similar but orange-billed.

name: Knob-billed Duck
rangeDescription: Tropical africa and madagascar; disjunctly india to southern china
description: Large bicolored waterbird. Both sexes are iridescent purplish-green above with a white or buffy breast.

name: Chestnut-headed Tanager
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay to southeastern brazil and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: A skulking tanager found in dense undergrowth of humid forests and second growth often with bamboo. Males have a chestnut head with a black forehead and mask, but are otherwise gray.

name: Beijing Babbler
rangeDescription: Central and northeastern china and northern korean peninsula
description: Long-tailed brown bird with a white throat, streaked back, and rusty belly. Inhabits dry vegetation, ranging from scrub to tall grasses to reedbeds.

name: Cundinamarca Antpitta
rangeDescription: Eastern andes of colombia (cundinamarca and meta)
description: A rather plain antpitta known only from a small area of Colombia’s eastern Andes, southeast of Bogotá. Plumage is dull brown with small white streaks on the underparts, a slightly paler belly, and a faint eyering.

name: Plain Sunbird
rangeDescription: Southern myanmar to malaya, sumatra including nias, borneo, and north natuna islands
description: A medium-large sunbird with a rather thick, slightly decurved bill. Extremely plain: pale olive-yellow above and paler washed-out yellow below.

name: Malabar Gray Hornbill
rangeDescription: Moist deciduous forest of southwestern india
description: A small gray hornbill with a casque-less pale bill, a black undertail with white tips, and a pale eyebrow. Sexes are alike, except that the females have black on the base of the bill.

name: Arctic Tern
rangeDescription: Arctic circumpolar; winters sub-antarctic and antarctic seas
description: Elegant seabird with extremely long wings and forked tail. Adults are pale gray with white cheek, black cap, and red bill and legs.

name: Swinhoe's Pheasant
rangeDescription: Montane forest of central taiwan
description: Secretive, handsome endemic pheasant of Taiwan's mountains. Male slaty blue from nape to flanks, with contrasting white upper back, brown mantle, and dark gray wings; female mostly rich brown with pale markings above.

name: Dull-mantled Antbird
rangeDescription: Caribbean slope of eastern costa rica and both slopes of panama
description: Medium-sized antbird with plump body and short tail. Gray body and brown back.

name: Peruvian Recurvebill
rangeDescription: Tropical southeastern peru, far northwestern bolivia, and amazonian brazil
description: Reddish-brown bird with a distinctive upturned bill. Found almost exclusively in bamboo thickets, but occasionally also in dense viny areas.

name: Fire-fronted Bishop
rangeDescription: Southwestern somalia to eastern kenya and far northeastern tanzania
description: Breeding males are beautiful and unmistakable, with black-and-yellow plumage and a distinctive red forehead patch. Females and non-breeding males are brown and streaky.

name: Black-necked Wattle-eye
rangeDescription: Humid forest of southern cameroon and gabon; bioko
description: A distinctive wattle-eye with iridescent blue-black upperparts and throat, off-white underparts, and bright green eye wattles. Unlike many other wattle-eyes, sexes are similar, with the female looking like a male with dull plumage.

name: Toro Olive-Greenbul
rangeDescription: Southern south sudan, eastern democratic republic of the congo, uganda, far western kenya, and far northwestern tanzania
description: A drab, long-tailed brownish greenbul. The upperparts are brown and the underparts paler olive-gray.
